title: Presheaves of rings and their sheafifications are ring objects
statement:
Let $C$ be a site as in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] (for instance $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
or the site of profinite sets), with abelian presheaves carrying the objectwise tensor product
$\otimes_p$ and abelian sheaves the tensor product
$\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G=a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)$ of
[det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure].

1. A presheaf of rings $P$ on $C$ is a ring object of abelian presheaves, with multiplication and
   unit given at each $U$ by those of the ring $P(U)$ ([det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings]).
   A morphism of presheaves of rings is a morphism of ring objects. If all $P(U)$ are commutative,
   the ring object $P$ is commutative.
2. The sheafification $aP$ of the underlying abelian presheaf of $P$ is a ring object of
   $\Sh(C,\Ab)$, with multiplication $aP\otimes aP\cong a(P\otimes_pP)\xrightarrow{a\mu}aP$ and unit
   $\underline{\mathbf Z}=a(\underline{\mathbf Z})\xrightarrow{a\eta}aP$; it is commutative when all
   $P(U)$ are, and $a$ sends morphisms of presheaves of rings to morphisms of ring objects.

proof.text: For an arrow $u\colon V\to U$ of $C$, write $r_u\colon P(U)\to P(V)$ for restriction. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings], $r_u\mu_{P(U)}=\mu_{P(V)}(r_u\otimes r_u)$ and $r_u\eta_{P(U)}=\eta_{P(V)}$. The tensor restrictions are $r_u\otimes r_u$ and the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z$ has identity restrictions, by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf], part 1. These two equalities are precisely the naturality conditions, so the objectwise maps define natural transformations $\mu\colon P\otimes_pP\to P$ and $\eta\colon\underline{\mathbf Z}\to P$.

source.place: proof, part 1: construction and naturality of multiplication and unit

proof.text: The associator and both unitors of the presheaf tensor product have the corresponding components in $\Ab$, by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf], part 1. Thus each of the three ring-object equations of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], part 1, evaluated at $U$, is exactly the corresponding equation for $(P(U),\mu_{P(U)},\eta_{P(U)})$, which holds by [det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings], part 1. Natural transformations are equal when their components are equal, so these equations hold for $P$. If every $P(U)$ is commutative, objectwise symmetry gives $(\mu\circ\beta_{P,P})_U=\mu_{P(U)}\circ\beta_{P(U),P(U)}=\mu_{P(U)}$ by part 3 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings]. Componentwise equality therefore gives $\mu\circ\beta_{P,P}=\mu$, the commutativity condition in part 3 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid].

source.place: proof, part 1: objectwise ring-object axioms and commutativity

proof.text: Let $f\colon P\to Q$ be a morphism of presheaves of rings, and use the structures just constructed for $P$ and $Q$. Each $f_U$ is a ring homomorphism, so [det-def-sfb-ring-object-rings], part 2, gives $f_U\mu_{P(U)}=\mu_{Q(U)}(f_U\otimes f_U)$ and $f_U\eta_{P(U)}=\eta_{Q(U)}$. Tensoring morphisms is objectwise by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf], part 1. Consequently these are the components of $f\mu_P=\mu_Q(f\otimes_pf)$ and $f\eta_P=\eta_Q$; componentwise equality proves both natural-transformation identities. These are the morphism conditions of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], part 2.

source.place: proof, part 1: morphisms of presheaves of rings

proof.text: By the assertion in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], sheafification $a$ is strong symmetric monoidal for these tensor products, with tensor comparison $aP\otimes aP\cong a(P\otimes_pP)$ and unit $\mathbf1_{\Sh}=a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$, the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z}$. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], part 1, to $F=a$ and the ring object $P$ constructed above: its multiplication is $a\mu$ after this tensor comparison and its unit is $a\eta$ after this unit comparison, exactly as stated. Its image of any morphism $f$ from the preceding step is $a(f)$, a morphism of ring objects. The symmetric monoidal functor is braided, so part 2 of the same transport theorem applies to a commutative $P$ and makes $aP$ commutative. No sectionwise identification of sheaf tensor products is used.

source.place: proof, part 2: apply monoidal and braided transport to sheafification

proof_origin.place: parts 1 and 2; the component verifications in part 1 are expanded
